trust_decision.summary: The unauthenticated MDM /profile handler decides whether a PKCS#7-signed plist really comes from an Apple-issued device identity before it rebinds the device record's UDID by SERIAL and issues a fresh OCO device identity (cert + private key in a .p12). At the pinned commit it verifies with PKCS7_NOVERIFY, so any self-signed signer is accepted.

landing_point.why: The summary names the /profile endpoint and PKCS7_NOVERIFY. That literal appears once, in the /profile branch of api-mdm.php, next to a comment explaining why chain checking was disabled.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /api-mdm.php/profile (unauthenticated device enrollment; fix.diff:75-92, follow-up parse fix fix.diff:57-59)

POST /api-mdm.php/profile, via the new helper checkiPhoneCaSignature appended after checkSignature (fix.diff:101-125): openssl cms -verify against the Apple Root CA, with -no_check_time and -purpose sslclient
fix_sites.module_kind: verification helper in the same file

fix_sites.entry_point: the trust-anchor constants APPLE_ROOT_CA_FILE and APPLE_WDR_CA_FILE plus the new PEM asset files, used by the /profile helper (fix.diff:200-201, fix.diff:126-191)

generateMdmApnCsr() (admin MDM settings, APN CSR signing): the inline APPLE_CERT_CHAIN constant is replaced with the new PEM files (fix.diff:210-214, fix.diff:222-275). This is a refactor, not part of the flaw.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The only change outside api-mdm.php moves the Apple CA chain from an inline constant (lib/Apple/AutomatedDeviceEnrollment.class.php:133) into asset files. It is a refactor and does not close any route into the flaw.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the O8 signer-to-device binding gap in checkSignature (/checkin, /mdm): 'those routes already verify the CMS chain against the OCO device CA (frontend/api-mdm.php:482); the advisory is about /profile accepting self-signed signatures, and the CN check is an existing TODO feature (frontend/api-mdm.php:477).'

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Real iPhones sign /profile requests with an Apple iPhone Device CA chain whose CA cert has expired, so the fix must keep accepting that chain while ignoring validity time. An over-broad fix (strict time validation, or requiring the OCO device CA as for checkSignature) breaks genuine ADE enrollment. Separately, the admin-authenticated .mobileconfig download must keep calling generateEnrollmentProfile without any signature.

O6_input_shapes: DER PKCS#7/CMS SignedData with embedded content (the published fix uses -inform DER, read from stdin)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /checkin Authenticate/TokenUpdate/CheckOut: checkSignature verifies only that the signer chains to the OCO device CA and never binds the signer CN to the SerialNumber/UDID in the body (explicit TODO), so any enrolled identity can rewrite another device's record
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The chain is verified (frontend/api-mdm.php:482); the advisory is about self-signed /profile signatures, not about cross-device binding on /checkin.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, about 400 lines below the landing point; the updates are at frontend/api-mdm.php:108-118, 149-159, 179-186

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /mdm command results: the same unbound checkSignature, then the device is selected by the body UDID and its info, apps and profiles are updated
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The /mdm channel is post-enrollment command traffic, a neighbouring feature, and the signature is already checked.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /profile after the published fix: the Apple-chain check does not bind the signer certificate to the SERIAL in the signed plist, so a valid Apple-chained signer can still request another serial's enrollment identity
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The report only says 'accepts self-signed signatures'; once the chain is verified a solver will treat the request as trusted.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second embedded-signature verifier for a planted macOS/User-enrollment profile route that reuses openssl_pkcs7_verify with PKCS7_NOVERIFY
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The author already wrote two verifiers in this file and justified NOVERIFY with an expired Apple CA comment (frontend/api-mdm.php:43). A copy for another enrollment flow is plausible.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a library-level helper (e.g. enrollment from a signed request) in the ADE class that parses the signed plist itself and calls generateEnrollmentProfile, placed in another file from the handler
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The ADE class already wraps openssl CLI calls (lib/Apple/AutomatedDeviceEnrollment.class.php:447-456) and owns enrollment-profile generation, so moving request parsing there is a natural refactor.

O9_family: signature/certificate-chain verification disabled (CWE-295) leading to device-identity issuance and device-record takeover

O10_build.toolchain: PHP with openssl ext + /usr/bin/openssl CLI (both verifiers shell out to it), composer-free vendored CFPropertyList, phpunit (tests/phpunit.xml)
O10_build.project_tests: tests/MobileDeviceTest.php covers only mobileconfig placeholder templating; there are no tests for api-mdm.php signature verification, and the fix adds none.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Drop PKCS7_NOVERIFY and pass the Apple root as CA to openssl_pkcs7_verify. This fails on the expired iPhone Device CA, so the tempting follow-up is to fall back or verify against the OCO device CA; neither binds the signer to the SERIAL.

out_of_scope_notes: frontend/api-mdm.php:295-298 uses an undefined $deviceCertCn instead of $certInfo['subject']['CN'], so the /parameters lookup is broken (a functional bug, not pursued).
Predictable shared /tmp paths for the device private key and p12 (lib/Apple/AutomatedDeviceEnrollment.class.php:442-446) and for the request files (frontend/api-mdm.php:33-34).
The unauthenticated ?enterpriseToken= branch creates an Android enterprise when none exists (frontend/api-mdm.php:445-456).
frontend/api-mdm.php:6 logs every raw MDM request body at debug level.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell); the project looks small (single PHP app), so tiny_repo (<5 MB of source) may apply and was not confirmed.
Whether the O8 routes (missing CN binding in checkSignature, no SERIAL binding on /profile) are still present in the latest code: no latest release given.

Whether openssl cms -purpose sslclient with -partial_chain on the Apple Root CA accepts non-device Apple-chained certs (e.g. developer certs) was not evaluated; this bears on whether the third O8 route is exploitable as described.

docs/Mobile-Device-Management.md:102 says device-certificate authentication is 'done in all MDM API requests'. This weakens but does not remove the reason to dismiss for the O8 routes; not counted as protection_documented_without_exceptions because the CN-to-device binding is not documented.

Pattern B is weak: O8 relies on identity binding (a how-type gap) flagged by the author's own TODO at frontend/api-mdm.php:477, which a solver may notice; the published fix itself is effectively a single-location change.
